notes: Non-blocking. Judged in full at gate 990243026f1289fb, as if for the first time; the filings filing.json and filing-2.json of this folder were made at older gates and are history. I have no open finding to release or re-raise (round-1 F1 is closed). (1) work/Names3.lean prints the claim with full names and explicit instances: every operation of the model is TVA.* (tl.program_id, tl.arange, tl.load, tl.add, tl.store, Tensor.ltS, IntV.ofNat, IntV.instMul, Tensor.instHAddIntV, instHAddPtrTensorIntV, Prog.instMonad), the grid formula uses core Nat.instDiv, instSubNat and instAddNat, and the only other kernel constant is the generated proof add_kernel._proof_1 of the Fin 3 literal 0. Lean prints the do block's non-dependent lets as have; the meaning is the same (body_eq is rfl). main, consistent and satisfiable use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. (2) Since my last acceptance the library changed Format.nanMag and Format.toRat, which Post's FloatV.add reaches; work/AddCheck3.lean (generated by work/f32add.py) evaluates FloatV.add on 600 float32 pairs (21 chosen: ties to even both ways, overflow to +inf and the tie at maxVal, inf + -inf, signed zeros, subnormals kept, NaN operands, 1 + 2^-10 exact; 579 random) and finds all equal to numpy's float32 addition and to an exact rounding of the rational sum, NaN results compared as NaN. So Post is the IEEE float32 sum and rejects a bfloat16-precision or flushing kernel. (3) work/Cover3.lean proves Inst.ok for the host's shape (fresh disjoint float32 buffers, BLOCK_SIZE = 1024) at n = 98432, 2^12 and 2^27, at the edges n = 0, 1 and 2^31 - 1 (BLOCK_SIZE = 1 and 2^20), and for add(x, x); it fails at n = 2^31 and for an in-place output, as the README says; the grid formula gives triton.cdiv at those sizes, and launch keeps debug = false, fusion = true, numCtas = 1, pdl = false, blocks [[BLOCK_SIZE]]. (4) work/Checks3.lean: IntV.ofNat B is IntV.ofInt B in int32 (line 44's note), the n = 1 constant is IntV.ofNat 1, program_id axis 0 is the program's number, and on offsets and n in [0, 2^31) the signed int32 comparison of line 47 is the comparison of the numbers. (5) Part (A) of Compiler.Faithful's scope against the script's launches (line 75, called at 89 and through triton.testing.do_bench at 127): no launch option or warmup or triton.compile, no autotune or heuristics, a bare @triton.jit, no descriptor, no host TensorDescriptor, no CUDA graph capture (do_bench, not do_bench_cudagraph; no torch.cuda.graph). Module-level names: the launch reads only tl and triton (lines 23-24, kernel lines, mapped); the host lines bind torch, DEVICE, add, size, x, y, output_torch, output_triton and benchmark, none of which the kernel reads (its x, y are assigned at lines 50-51 before line 52 reads them), and add's annotations and benchmark's decorator (whose list comprehension binds no module-level name) bind nothing. (6) Wording only: README, The supported subset, says the operators are on int32 and float32 values; the + of lines 50, 51 and 54 adds an int32 block to a *fp32 pointer (the map entries say so).
